name: Duplicate environment variable
description: A container with duplicate environment variable names can behave unexpectedly because later values override earlier values. Duplicate entries usually indicate configuration drift or copy-paste mistakes.
long_description: Defining duplicate environment variable names within the same container specification creates ambiguity. In Kubernetes container runtimes, when multiple environment variables share the same name, the last defined occurrence silently overrides earlier definitions. This typically indicates copy-paste errors or merge mistakes, and can mask intended configuration values or security settings. Ensuring unique environment variable keys maintains clear configuration intent and prevents subtle runtime bugs.
remediation: Remove or rename duplicate environment variable entries so each container defines each environment variable name only once.
test: Check every container in Pods, pod-template workloads, and CronJobs for repeated env[].name values within the same container.
